problem: End-to-end DRL ObjNav policies, including graph-based ones, plan implicitly from immediate visual context. They lack explicit hierarchical guidance and progress feedback, and generalize poorly to unseen scenes and long-horizon search. LLM-based navigators bring commonsense but need frequent, costly LLM queries at runtime.
motivation: Human navigation relies on hierarchical semantic reasoning, but LLMs lack spatial grounding and are too slow to call at every step. The paper grounds LLM planning in hierarchical scene graphs. It distills the plan into dense embeddings for a lightweight reactive RL policy, keeping control latency low.
key_idea: An LLM plans semantic waypoints asynchronously over a retrieved hierarchical scene-graph subgraph. An R-GCN encoder (HSGE) turns the waypoints into embeddings, and an alignment-gated fusion network (GAFN) merges them with egocentric vision for an A3C policy.
insight: Decoupling sparse asynchronous LLM planning from a fast reactive policy gives competitive accuracy with far lower latency (0.42 s vs 2.20 s for CogNav, 9.1 LLM calls per episode). In the zero-shot ablation, removing alignment fusion hurts most (SR 75.05 to 70.65). Removing LLM reasoning (73.30) or unseen inference (73.84) also lowers SR, so both commonsense priors and fusion matter. Removing GAFN slightly raises SPL, indicating its gating acts as a conservative constraint that trades some efficiency for robustness.
method: Hierarchical Scene Graph Builder: incrementally builds an object/cluster hierarchy with a hybrid spatial (Gaussian) and semantic (cosine) similarity. Cluster summaries are VLM-generated and refreshed only on semantic drift. Edges are intra-level spatial and inter-level inclusion.

Retrieval-Augmented Compact Subgraph: scores nodes by instruction similarity, ancestor gain and neighborhood boosting, then keeps the top-K nodes as the subgraph G_Q. Re-planning is triggered only on subgoal attainment or deadlock.

LLM Global Planner: formulated as a TSPP with a coherence weight (semantic minus geometric distance) solved by Greedy-TSPP. Regional plans are grounded to object waypoints, and unseen targets get a virtual node at the most compatible cluster's centroid.
HSGE: a 3-layer R-GCN with residual per level, waypoint-conditioned residual attention, and level-wise average pooling plus MLP, producing a 64-D waypoint embedding E_w.

GAFN: cross-attention with visual features as query and E_w as key/value. A gated fusion uses cosine alignment α_t and a penalty (1-η σ(κ α_t)) so reliance shifts to structural context as alignment rises.
A3C RL policy: two-layer LSTM actor-critic on the fused feature, with a shaped reward (visibility, forward, distance progress, step penalty). Training uses scene graphs pre-built offline.

setting.backbone: Frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 + Qwen2.5-VL-7B (planner, frozen) + trained R-GCN HSGE/GAFN/LSTM A3C policy
setting.model_size: 7B LLM planner plus small trained policy modules
setting.training_data: A3C RL in AI2-THOR iTHOR (20 scenes per room type train) and RoboTHOR (60 apartments train), 6M episodes; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (CLIP features) with online 3D scene graph from OpenSEED segmentation, and a detector
setting.privileged: Scene graphs of training environments pre-constructed offline; at test time built online. Otherwise none.

numbers.eval_set_note: ALL trajectories; 1,000 test episodes, best validation checkpoint
six object categories unseen in training (Bowl, DeskLamp, Laptop, LightSwitch, Plate, StoveBurner)

numbers.extra: Latency 0.42 s per step, 9.1 LLM calls per episode
numbers.evidence: Table III performance vs efficiency in RoboTHOR

numbers_note: Benchmarks are iTHOR/RoboTHOR object-goal navigation (not in the canonical list). The split is labeled 'test' by the evaluator (the paper says 'test episodes'). The RoboTHOR efficiency table rounds the same numbers as Table I.
results: SAGE-Nav reaches SR 82.47 on iTHOR (vs TSOG 80.04; CGI-GAIL has higher SPL 46.25) and 52.35 SR / 30.12 SPL on RoboTHOR (vs TSOG 49.89 / 28.41). In zero-shot on unseen categories it gets 75.05 SR vs 69.51 for AKGVP-CI. It has the lowest latency (0.42 s) and fewest LLM calls (9.1) compared with CogNav (SR 54.6) and SG-Nav.
limitations: Failure cases: target visibility errors, detector false positives, entrapment in narrow starts, and premature termination.
Evaluated only in simulation (AI2-THOR), with no real-robot experiments despite claims of physical deployment readiness.
iTHOR SPL is below CGI-GAIL. Scene graphs for training scenes are built offline, and the pipeline depends on detector/segmentation quality.
